identity.name: Calcium phosphates
identity.chemical_class: Inorganic calcium salts of phosphoric acid (orthophosphates)

function.mechanism: Calcium phosphates regulate pH/buffering, reduce caking by improving powder flow, and provide acid-reacting/raising functionality in baked systems; some forms also contribute calcium/phosphorus fortification.
common_food_categories: infant formula and foods for infants/young children
processed foods using phosphate salts for texture and processing

adi.basis: EFSA 2019 group ADI for phosphates (including E341), expressed as phosphorus.

efsa.key_finding: EFSA concluded the group ADI is protective for healthy adults, but estimated exposure exceeded the ADI in several younger/high-consumer groups and the ADI does not apply to moderate-severe renal impairment.

adi.basis: JECFA calcium phosphate entries report a group MTDI of 70 mg/kg bw (as phosphorus) from all sources.

concerns.summary: EFSA identified renal calcification/tubular nephropathy as a key adverse effect in phosphate toxicology and noted the ADI does not apply to moderate-severe renal impairment.
A cohort study reported higher urinary phosphate associated with higher cardiovascular disease incidence, with interpretation linked to higher intake of highly processed foods.
A randomized cross-over study in healthy adults found meals containing inorganic phosphate additives altered acute calcium/phosphate homeostasis.
A 2025 mouse study observed anxiety-like behavior and neuroimmune changes under high dietary phosphate intake.

no_concern_confirmed: EFSA reported no concern for genotoxicity and carcinogenicity for the phosphate additive group in its 2019 re-evaluation.
FDA lists calcium phosphate as GRAS in 21 CFR 182.1217 when used under good manufacturing practice.
No specific IARC monograph classification entry for calcium phosphate was identified in the current IARC list dataset searched.

adi_exceedance.notes: EFSA analytical-data exposure scenario exceeded the 40 mg/kg bw/day group ADI in several younger populations; supplements were also noted as potentially exceeding ADI.

risk_assessment.rationale: E341 remains approved in major jurisdictions, but EFSA set a finite group ADI and documented exceedance in younger/high-exposure populations, with additional human and mechanistic studies supporting caution at higher inorganic phosphate intakes.
key_factors: EFSA 2019 group ADI: 40 mg/kg bw/day as phosphorus
Documented ADI exceedance in infants/toddlers/children and high-exposure groups
FDA GRAS status under 21 CFR 182.1217 with GMP condition
JECFA group MTDI 70 mg/kg bw (as P), evaluation year 1982
No IARC classification entry for calcium phosphate in the current IARC list dataset
